name: Permanent Resident visa (永住者)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 10 continuous years of residence in Japan, of which the most recent 5 years must include a valid, ongoing work status with genuine income.
This requires a stable, sufficient livelihood, and being fully current on tax and public pension/insurance payments — genuine, well-documented compliance is scrutinised closely.
requirements.fix_path: Ensure all tax and pension/insurance obligations are current before applying.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires holding Highly Skilled Professional status with 70+ points maintained for 3 years, or 80+ points maintained for 1 year.

requirement_groups.name: Spouse of Japanese national accelerated route

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being married to and residing with a Japanese national or permanent resident for a sufficient period (commonly cited around 3 years of marriage with at least 1 year of residence in Japan).

evidence_required.document: 10 (or accelerated) years of residence and tax/pension compliance evidence
Guarantor letter from a Japanese national or permanent resident

sources.title: Immigration Services Agency of Japan — 永住許可に関するガイドライン (Permanent Residence Guidelines, revised 24 February 2026, Reiwa 8)

notes: Japan's Eijusha hub route, same structural role as uk_ilr, de_niederlassungserlaubnis, and every other country's PR-hub route in this dataset — but with a genuinely long standard timeline (10 years) among the longest in this entire multi-country dataset, second only to some of Spain's/UK's slower non-CPLP tracks. Three groups modeled: standard 10-year track, and two accelerated tracks (HSP fast-track at 1-3 years depending on points, spouse-of-Japanese-national at ~3 years) using prerequisites_override — a clean, confirmed application of the schema's group-level prerequisites mechanism, same pattern as UK ILR's multi-group structure. citizenship_after_months (0) reflects that Japan's naturalisation residence clock (5 years) runs independently of PR status rather than being gated behind it — genuinely UNLIKE most European countries in this dataset (UK, Germany, Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, France all require holding PR/settlement before or as part of naturalisation eligibility) — someone could naturalise in Japan without ever holding PR at all, a real and significant structural distinction worth surfacing prominently in any cross-country comparison view. Permanent Residence Guidelines dated 24 February 2026 (Reiwa 8) confirm this is current, recently-reaffirmed policy, not a stale historical rule — same freshness confirmation as jp_highly_skilled_professional.
